subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty:true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or fail the tool call instead?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the requested behavior changes how a sandbox capability denial is surfaced, and the issue explicitly allows two security-boundary outcomes.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so users must choose a non-sandbox or elevated path for PTY-only commands.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Fork Fix
options.body: After deciding the behavior, review the open fork candidate or create a narrow replacement with tests and user-facing proof.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning when sandbox mode disables explicit PTY while preserving the current non-PTY sandbox execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history signal across exec PTY behavior, sandbox fallback semantics, and exec routing/docs changes.
